content:
I am an Assistant Professor in Machine Learning and Data Integration at the Faculty ITC, University of Twente. I build machine learning and computer vision pipelines for satellite imagery and spatiotemporal data, from detecting crops, open spaces, solar panels from space to benchmarking AI agents in QGIS. My teaching topics include scientific programming, machine learning, data science, ethics in relation to spatial data and GeoAI in the UNIGIS MSc - University of Twente and Vrije Universitait.
As a QGIS contributor and open-source advocate I maintain the ML4QGIS plugin. I have also contributed to the organization of FOSS4G/QGIS conferences and deliver talks and workshops. Before academia I was Deputy President of the Geographic Institute of Venezuela. I welcome collaboration with industry and government.
summary: I am an Assistant Professor in Machine Learning and Data Integration at the Faculty ITC, University of Twente. I build machine learning and computer vision pipelines for satellite imagery and spatiotemporal data, from detecting crops, open spaces, solar panels from space to benchmarking AI agents in QGIS. My teaching topics include scientific programming, machine learning, data science, ethics in relation to spatial data and GeoAI in the UNIGIS MSc - University of Twente and Vrije Universitait.
title: Rosa Aguilar

content:
ML4QGIS (Machine Learning for QGIS) brings machine learning for image classification and regression into QGIS, so geospatial analysts can train and apply models without writing code.
 Available in the official QGIS plugin repository (version 0.4.0, August 2026), with more than 6,000 downloads. Open source under GPL-3.0 on GitHub. Introduced at FOSS4GNL 2025 and used in the FOSS4G 2026 workshop GeoAI Level Up, including YOLO object detection inside ML4QGIS.  Feedback, issues and pull requests are welcome.
summary: A QGIS plugin for image classification and regression with machine learning, no coding needed. In the official QGIS plugin repository, with 6,000+ downloads.
title: ML4QGIS: machine learning inside QGIS

content:
AI agents are starting to operate GIS software on their own. How reliable are they on real geospatial tasks?
I lead the design of a benchmark that evaluates AI agents on geospatial tasks in QGIS. The benchmark questions are openly available on Zenodo.
summary: Designing a benchmark that tests how well AI agents carry out real geospatial tasks in QGIS.
title: Benchmarking AI agents for GIS

content: Built a YOLOv11 object-detection pipeline that detects solar panels in satellite imagery. Developed Python and Google Earth Engine workflows on VIIRS night-light imagery to identify rural areas lacking electricity access. Built ML-ready training datasets from multi-temporal satellite imagery and coordinated the field data collection used to label them.
summary: A YOLOv11 pipeline that detects solar panels in satellite imagery, combined with VIIRS night lights to find rural areas without electricity access.
title: Solar panels and electricity access from space

content:
Equitable access to green and public space is part of SDG 11.7, but up-to-date maps of public green spaces are rare, and existing approaches often depend on proprietary software.
This work builds a fully reproducible workflow using only Sentinel-2 imagery, OpenStreetMap data and open-source Python libraries, covering data acquisition, preprocessing, deep learning and evaluation.
Read the paper: City and Environment Interactions (2026).
summary: A fully reproducible deep learning workflow that maps public urban green spaces from Sentinel-2 imagery and OpenStreetMap with open-source Python tools.
title: Mapping public urban green spaces with open data

content:
Smart Monitoring for a Changing Climate: Machine Learning in Pollen Prediction.
Spatiotemporal machine learning to predict pollen, building on my work with Random Forest, Mixed Effects Random Forest, Prophet and SVM models for climate and Earth-system prediction. Presented at the NWO NAC conference (2026).
summary: Smart monitoring for a changing climate: spatiotemporal machine learning to predict pollen.
title: Machine learning for pollen prediction

content:
OGITO (Open Geospatial Interactive TOol) supports collaborative spatial planning on maptables: large horizontal touch screens that a group of stakeholders can use together.
 Co-designed with planners and stakeholders using human-centred design and agile development. Used for community mapping in Sumatra, Indonesia, and for noise action planning. Code on GitHub; dataset on Zenodo. Papers: CEUS 2020, Journal of Urban Technology 2023, and the PhD thesis.
summary: An open-source web tool that runs real-time spatial analysis on touch tables so stakeholders can plan together. Co-designed with its users.
title: OGITO: open tool for collaborative planning

summary: A fully open, reproducible deep learning workflow that maps public urban green spaces from Sentinel-2 imagery and OpenStreetMap data with open-source Python tools, supporting SDG 11.7.
title: A reproducible geospatial workflow for detecting public urban green spaces using open data

content: Our paper A reproducible geospatial workflow for detecting public urban green spaces using open data is out in City and Environment Interactions, with Pitchaporn Likitpanjamanon and Frank Ostermann. Read it (open access).
summary: Published in City and Environment Interactions: a fully reproducible deep learning workflow using Sentinel-2, OpenStreetMap and open-source Python.
title: New paper: mapping public urban green spaces with open data
